<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a `.nvchecker.toml` configuration file used by nvchecker, a standard tool for monitoring upstream releases. It simply declares that the `testx-bin` package should monitor the GitHub repository `whoisdinanath/testx` for new releases, stripping the `v` prefix from version tags.

There is no executable code, no network requests, no file operations, and no obfuscation. The file contains only declarative configuration metadata. It is not part of the build process itself but rather a maintainer convenience file for version tracking. This is entirely consistent with standard AUR packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard, well-formed AUR package for the "testx-bin" application. It follows conventional packaging practices with proper source handling through GitHub releases, verified SHA256 checksums for all architectures, and standard installation steps. The package simply builds and installs a universal test runner binary along with its documentation and license files. There are no signs of supply chain compromises, obfuscated code, unexpected network activity, or malicious behavior. The source URLs point to the official GitHub repository, and all checksums are explicitly provided (not skipped). The package performs only expected operations: copying the binary to /usr/bin, placing README and LICENSE files in their designated locations, and using appropriate permission flags (m755 for the binary, m644 for text files).

No suspicious elements are present. The file contains no hidden commands, no attempts to execute external code, and no deviations from standard AUR packaging workflows. The `options=("!strip")` directive is a common optimization for reducing binary size and is not indicative of any security issue.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>A standard AUR package with proper checksums and conventional installation procedures.</summary>
</security_assessment>
